**The last Republican elected governor of New York was George Pataki (1994).**  
On the 1994 ballot, Pataki appeared on **four party lines** (the so‑called “fusion” ballot lines used in New York):

| Ballot line | Party that endorsed the line | Source |
|-------------|------------------------------|--------|
| Republican | New York Republican Party | 1994 New York gubernatorial election infobox【1†L49-L54】 |
| Conservative | Conservative Party of New York State | 1994 New York gubernatorial election infobox【1†L49-L54】 |
| Tax Cut Now | Tax Cut Now Party (created by the GOP for 1994) | 1994 New York gubernatorial election infobox【1†L49-L54】 |
| Liberal | Liberal Party of New York | 1994 New York gubernatorial election infobox【1†L49-L54】 |

(An “alliance” entry in the infobox indicates the additional ballot lines that the nominee was listed on.)

So, when George Pataki was first elected governor in 1994, the parties under which he ran were:

- **Republican**
- **Conservative**
- **Tax Cut Now**
- **Liberal**

These lines together made up Pataki’s ballot appearance in that election.
